title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em araucária. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em guarujá. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em presidente prudente. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners. Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups. description:

Job Title:  Implementation Analyst English Resume Only  Location:  Brazil  Type:  Full-Time Contract  Setup:  Fully Remote  Level:  Mid-Level  Industry:  Software SAAS Company  Shift:  US Hours  Start Date:  can start in 2 weeks after offer  Equipment:  Available upon request  Rate:  R$8,000 - R$10,000 About The Methodical Group   The Methodical Group (methodicalgroup.com) is a leading global provider of IT Services, Consulting, and Specialized Staffing Solutions, operating with a systematic, high-quality approach for over 25 years. Headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, we use proprietary frameworks, such as Exact Talent®, to provide specialized workforce solutions, including permanent placement and contract staffing, across industries such as IT and Healthcare. Simultaneously, our IT and Business Services division offers expert solutions in Software Development, Data & Analytics, and IT Operations, aiming to help organizations worldwide drive digital transformation, improve efficiency, and maintain a competitive edge.  About the Opportunity   Our client is seeking an Implementation Analyst to support their Professional Services team, leading end-to-end deployments of a Saa S platform across municipal government clients. This role combines project leadership, client engagement, and product expertise—guiding customers through configuration, setup, data migration, and training to ensure successful system adoption.  The Implementation Analyst will work closely with clients to understand business requirements and translate them into scalable system solutions, ensuring each customer realizes measurable value while delivering a seamless and high-quality onboarding experience.  Responsibilities   Lead the full implementation lifecycle for new customers, from kickoff through go-live, managing multiple concurrent implementations for small-to-mid-sized municipal clients.  Conduct discovery sessions to gather business requirements, workflows, and success metrics, translating them into system configurations.  Configure and customize the Saa S platform based on client-specific use cases while maintaining best practices and scalability.  Coordinate with Data Engineers on data imports and integrations, performing QA testing to validate functionality and data integrity prior to go-live.  Deliver customer training sessions to ensure user adoption and proficiency across departments.  Monitor project timelines, proactively managing scope, risks, dependencies, and overall project health.  Document configurations, implementation decisions, and knowledge base materials to support consistency and scalability.  Collaborate with Product, Support, and Customer Success teams to ensure smooth transition and ongoing client success post-launch.  Identify opportunities for process improvement and recommend best practices to optimize future implementations.    Qualifications   At least 2 years of Professional Services or Implementation experience supporting Enterprise Saa S products.  Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.  Strong understanding of Saa S platforms, cloud environments, and data management principles.  Working knowledge of data concepts such as file formats, field mapping, and data validation, with the ability to coordinate effectively with technical teams.  Experience using tools such as Wrike, Hub Spot, Salesforce, Jira, or similar implementation and project tracking platforms.  Proven experience working directly with clients and managing multiple implementation projects simultaneously.  Ability to manage client relationships professionally, set expectations, and communicate effectively throughout the project lifecycle.  Strong ability to translate technical concepts into clear, business-friendly language.  Excellent problem-solving, analytical, communication, organizational, and time-management skills.  Ability to quickly learn new technologies, tools, and business domains.

title: Web3 & al investment analyst
description:

Web3 DXB  is a Dubai-based investment and research platform focused on identifying and scaling high-potential opportunities at the intersection of  blockchain, artificial intelligence, and next-generation digital infrastructure  . We combine deep market insight with an agile, thesis-driven approach to back transformative technologies shaping the future of finance and the internet.  As we expand our investment activities, we are looking for a highly analytical and forward-thinking  Web3 & AI Investment Analyst  to join our team. This is a  fully remote position (Poland-based) , offering direct exposure to early-stage deals, market research, and high-impact investment decisions across Web3 and AI.  This role is ideal for someone who lives at the edge of innovation — tracking narratives, identifying asymmetric opportunities, and translating complex trends into actionable investment insights.   What You’ll Be Doing  Conduct deep-dive research on Web3 and AI sectors, including protocols, startups, and emerging technologies.  Analyze market trends, narratives, and macro developments across crypto and AI ecosystems.  Evaluate investment opportunities, including token projects, early-stage startups, and infrastructure plays.  Build investment theses and present insights to internal stakeholders.  Monitor portfolio performance and track key metrics across projects.  Collaborate with internal teams on strategy, deal flow, and market positioning.  Stay ahead of industry developments, identifying early signals and high-potential opportunities.     What We’re Looking For  2–4+ years of experience in investment analysis, research, venture capital, or crypto/AI markets.  Strong understanding of blockchain, De Fi, tokenomics, and Web3 ecosystems. title: Technical product owner
description:
Empresa está contratando Technical product owner em taubaté. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

ABOUT US  Syniti  , part of Capgemini, tackles the hardest work in data for the world’s largest organizations. We combine intelligent software with deep data expertise to help the Fortune2000 tackle complex data challenges and drive measurable business outcomes with business-ready data.  Syniti’s Data First strategy transforms data from an afterthought into a strategic asset—unlocking insights, reducing risk, and fueling growth. With over 5,000 successful projects, we support the full data lifecycle through a unified platform for migration, quality, replication, matching, master data management, analytics, governance, and strategy.  Operating globally across industries, Syniti’s award-winning software, expert consultants give enterprises a unique edge in managing and maximizing their data.  Syniti’s cloud-native platform sets new standards in enterprise data management, combining powerful Saa S solutions with deep domain expertise. Designed for agility and scale, our technology helps customers accelerate digital transformation, drive innovation, and make confident decisions with trusted data. Every product enhancement is built to solve real business challenges—empowering organizations to unlock value from their data faster and more effectively.  THE ROLE   We are seeking a highly technical and execution‑driven  Technical Product Owner  to serve as the “engine room” of our platform. In this role, you will translate high‑level product strategy into clear, actionable, and technically sound work for engineering teams. You will bridge complex legacy ERP architectures (SAP S/4 HANA, ECC) with modern, cloud‑native, AI‑driven workflows across the Syniti Knowledge Platform. This role goes far beyond writing tickets — we are looking for someone who uses AI for deep research, builds mockup screens to define user journeys, and ensures the creation of the “Golden Record” through seamless end‑to‑end integration across cataloging, migration, quality, and governance.  What You’ll Do   Product Ownership & Agile Execution: Lead 2–3 scrum teams by owning and prioritizing the backlog for key SKP capabilities (Migrate, Replicate, Drive, Orchestrate). Run high-impact backlog grooming, sprint planning, and estimation sessions.  Modern Requirement Engineering: Translate strategy into crisp Epics and User Stories. Use AI-driven tools to accelerate documentation, explore ERP integration patterns, and generate edge-case test scenarios.  UX & Workflow Prototyping: Design mockups and wireframes (Figma, v0, Miro) to visualize data journeys. Ensure that both Data Stewards and Developers experience intuitive, world‑class workflows within SKP.  Lifecycle Integration: Partner with Architecture and Engineering to define functional and non‑functional requirements (scalability, security). Ensure seamless integration across the entire data lifecycle to eliminate duplication and unlock full platform value.  Quality & Acceptance: Collaborate with the PXQ team to define “What Good Looks Like.” Act as the final validation gate to ensure features meet enterprise standards and align with real‑world user behavior.  Operational Feedback Loop: Engage with Support and Customer Success to funnel production learnings into the backlog, ensuring continuous improvement based on real customer usage.    WHAT IT TAKES   The Technical Veteran: 5+ years as a Product Owner or Business Analyst working on enterprise data products. Strong understanding of data integration, replication, APIs, and cloud-native architectures (AWS/Azure).  The ERP Expert: Deep experience with SAP ecosystems and large-scale transformation programs. Understanding of MDM, Data Quality, and Governance “plumbing.” Experience with SAP MDG or Informatica is a major plus.  The Modern Builder: An AI-native thinker who uses LLMs to enhance productivity and research. Prefers mockups over long documents and thrives in visual communication.  The Agile Leader: CSPO-certified with demonstrated ability to manage risks, dependencies, and scope changes across distributed, multi-time‑zone teams.  The Academic: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related practical experience.  The Communicator: Able to clearly articulate complex data and replication logic to business users while also explaining product vision to engineering teams.    Key Skills    Visionary Leadership:  Ability to maintain a clear product vision, define objectives, and mentor teams toward business goals.   Advanced Governance Concepts:  Strong command of data management and governance principles, including hierarchy and survivorship rules.   AI/ML Application:  Experience using AI/ML tools for documentation automation, market trend analysis, and optimization of data‑matching or data‑cleansing logic.   Visual Communication:  Skilled at producing wireframes and process flows to ensure UX alignment.   Technical Storyboarding:  Ability to write precise user stories and acceptance criteria with zero ambiguity.   Relationship Orchestration:  Strong interpersonal skills to influence stakeholders and drive collaborative engagement.  Drive for Results:  Relentless focus on delivering incremental value and ensuring release readiness in a fast‑moving environment.    Be fully aligned with our core values:  Think Big  - Be courageous and bold. Aspire to greatness. Relentlessly pursue market innovation. Set the standard by which others follow. Create solutions that have a meaningful impact. Solve the challenges our customers don’t know they have.  Be Curious  - Be a lifelong learner. Seek out new ideas to serve customers. Understand our competition and the world. Be permanently dissatisfied with the status quo. Challenge preconceptions. Focus on the future rather than yesterday.  Take Action  - Be the first. Don’t wait. Take accountability. Inspire others by doing. Fail fast and learn from mistakes. Make a difference every day.  Stronger Together  - Respect, trust and look out for each other. Celebrate diverse perspectives. Listen. Build connections and belonging. Act with integrity. Give back. One Syniti family.  By applying for this position, you acknowledge and consent to your image being captured (video or screenshot) for employment purposes, including during the hiring and onboarding process.   WHAT WE OFFER   Trust that you are proficient at what you do. At Syniti, you will find a supportive environment and access to learning tools, but micromanagement is not our thing.  Growth. We are growing rapidly and steadily solving the biggest challenges enterprise companies are faced with today. There was never a better time to join and grow with us. Most importantly, you will have the chance to shape our journey and share in our success story.  Support. We all rely on each other and enable each other to be successful. You won’t stand alone.  Curiosity and genuine interest in you. We all have our different stories, all equally fascinating, with each depicting a different journey, and we want to hear them all.  Recognition. We are the sum of individual achievements, and we always take the time to celebrate them.  An open organisation. Hierarchies are not our thing, and access is something we make sure of across the board. We are a family where everyone is just as important, everyone’s work is seen, and ideas are valued.    OUR COMMITMENT TO INCLUSION  At Syniti, we’re committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and fair workplace where everyone belongs and thrives. We believe that diverse perspectives make us stronger — and we value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and voices each person brings to our team.  We welcome applicants based on their skills and potential, and we’re dedicated to ensuring equal opportunities for all, regardless of personal background. If you need accommodations during the hiring process, please let us know — we’re here to support you.

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em itapecerica da serra. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position. title: Technical product owner
description:
Confira a vaga para Technical product owner em caieiras. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

ABOUT US  Syniti  , part of Capgemini, tackles the hardest work in data for the world’s largest organizations. We combine intelligent software with deep data expertise to help the Fortune2000 tackle complex data challenges and drive measurable business outcomes with business-ready data.  Syniti’s Data First strategy transforms data from an afterthought into a strategic asset—unlocking insights, reducing risk, and fueling growth. With over 5,000 successful projects, we support the full data lifecycle through a unified platform for migration, quality, replication, matching, master data management, analytics, governance, and strategy.  Operating globally across industries, Syniti’s award-winning software, expert consultants give enterprises a unique edge in managing and maximizing their data.  Syniti’s cloud-native platform sets new standards in enterprise data management, combining powerful Saa S solutions with deep domain expertise. Designed for agility and scale, our technology helps customers accelerate digital transformation, drive innovation, and make confident decisions with trusted data. Every product enhancement is built to solve real business challenges—empowering organizations to unlock value from their data faster and more effectively.  THE ROLE   We are seeking a highly technical and execution‑driven  Technical Product Owner  to serve as the “engine room” of our platform. In this role, you will translate high‑level product strategy into clear, actionable, and technically sound work for engineering teams. You will bridge complex legacy ERP architectures (SAP S/4 HANA, ECC) with modern, cloud‑native, AI‑driven workflows across the Syniti Knowledge Platform. This role goes far beyond writing tickets — we are looking for someone who uses AI for deep research, builds mockup screens to define user journeys, and ensures the creation of the “Golden Record” through seamless end‑to‑end integration across cataloging, migration, quality, and governance.  What You’ll Do   Product Ownership & Agile Execution: Lead 2–3 scrum teams by owning and prioritizing the backlog for key SKP capabilities (Migrate, Replicate, Drive, Orchestrate). Run high-impact backlog grooming, sprint planning, and estimation sessions.  Modern Requirement Engineering: Translate strategy into crisp Epics and User Stories. Use AI-driven tools to accelerate documentation, explore ERP integration patterns, and generate edge-case test scenarios.  UX & Workflow Prototyping: Design mockups and wireframes (Figma, v0, Miro) to visualize data journeys. Ensure that both Data Stewards and Developers experience intuitive, world‑class workflows within SKP.  Lifecycle Integration: Partner with Architecture and Engineering to define functional and non‑functional requirements (scalability, security). Ensure seamless integration across the entire data lifecycle to eliminate duplication and unlock full platform value.  Quality & Acceptance: Collaborate with the PXQ team to define “What Good Looks Like.” Act as the final validation gate to ensure features meet enterprise standards and align with real‑world user behavior.  Operational Feedback Loop: Engage with Support and Customer Success to funnel production learnings into the backlog, ensuring continuous improvement based on real customer usage.    WHAT IT TAKES   The Technical Veteran: 5+ years as a Product Owner or Business Analyst working on enterprise data products. Strong understanding of data integration, replication, APIs, and cloud-native architectures (AWS/Azure).  The ERP Expert: Deep experience with SAP ecosystems and large-scale transformation programs. Understanding of MDM, Data Quality, and Governance “plumbing.” Experience with SAP MDG or Informatica is a major plus.  The Modern Builder: An AI-native thinker who uses LLMs to enhance productivity and research. Prefers mockups over long documents and thrives in visual communication.  The Agile Leader: CSPO-certified with demonstrated ability to manage risks, dependencies, and scope changes across distributed, multi-time‑zone teams.  The Academic: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related practical experience.  The Communicator: Able to clearly articulate complex data and replication logic to business users while also explaining product vision to engineering teams.    Key Skills    Visionary Leadership:  Ability to maintain a clear product vision, define objectives, and mentor teams toward business goals.   Advanced Governance Concepts:  Strong command of data management and governance principles, including hierarchy and survivorship rules.   AI/ML Application:  Experience using AI/ML tools for documentation automation, market trend analysis, and optimization of data‑matching or data‑cleansing logic.   Visual Communication:  Skilled at producing wireframes and process flows to ensure UX alignment.   Technical Storyboarding:  Ability to write precise user stories and acceptance criteria with zero ambiguity.   Relationship Orchestration:  Strong interpersonal skills to influence stakeholders and drive collaborative engagement.  Drive for Results:  Relentless focus on delivering incremental value and ensuring release readiness in a fast‑moving environment.    Be fully aligned with our core values:  Think Big  - Be courageous and bold. Aspire to greatness. Relentlessly pursue market innovation. Set the standard by which others follow. Create solutions that have a meaningful impact. Solve the challenges our customers don’t know they have.  Be Curious  - Be a lifelong learner. Seek out new ideas to serve customers. Understand our competition and the world. Be permanently dissatisfied with the status quo. Challenge preconceptions. Focus on the future rather than yesterday.  Take Action  - Be the first. Don’t wait. Take accountability. Inspire others by doing. Fail fast and learn from mistakes. Make a difference every day.  Stronger Together  - Respect, trust and look out for each other. Celebrate diverse perspectives. Listen. Build connections and belonging. Act with integrity. Give back. One Syniti family.  By applying for this position, you acknowledge and consent to your image being captured (video or screenshot) for employment purposes, including during the hiring and onboarding process.   WHAT WE OFFER   Trust that you are proficient at what you do. At Syniti, you will find a supportive environment and access to learning tools, but micromanagement is not our thing.  Growth. We are growing rapidly and steadily solving the biggest challenges enterprise companies are faced with today. There was never a better time to join and grow with us. Most importantly, you will have the chance to shape our journey and share in our success story.  Support. We all rely on each other and enable each other to be successful. You won’t stand alone.  Curiosity and genuine interest in you. We all have our different stories, all equally fascinating, with each depicting a different journey, and we want to hear them all.  Recognition. We are the sum of individual achievements, and we always take the time to celebrate them.  An open organisation. Hierarchies are not our thing, and access is something we make sure of across the board. We are a family where everyone is just as important, everyone’s work is seen, and ideas are valued.    OUR COMMITMENT TO INCLUSION  At Syniti, we’re committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and fair workplace where everyone belongs and thrives. We believe that diverse perspectives make us stronger — and we value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and voices each person brings to our team.  We welcome applicants based on their skills and potential, and we’re dedicated to ensuring equal opportunities for all, regardless of personal background. If you need accommodations during the hiring process, please let us know — we’re here to support you.

title: Salesforce business system analyst
description:
Empresa está contratando Salesforce business system analyst em caxias do sul. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

Job Title: Salesforce Business Systems Analyst (BSA)  Location: LATAM   Duration: 6-12months   Job Summary:   We are looking for a  Salesforce Business Systems Analyst (BSA) with strong experience in gathering business requirements, translating them into functional specifications, and supporting Salesforce implementation and enhancements. The ideal candidate will work closely with business stakeholders, product owners, and technical teams to deliver scalable Salesforce solutions that support business processes.  Key Responsibilities:   ·Work with business stakeholders to  gather, analyze, and document business requirements  for Salesforce implementations and enhancements.  ·Translate business needs into  functional requirements, user stories, and process flows  .  ·Act as a  bridge between business teams and technical teams  to ensure accurate implementation of requirements.  ·Configure and support Salesforce features including  Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, workflows, validation rules, reports, and dashboards  .  ·Participate in  solution design discussions  and recommend best practices within the Salesforce ecosystem.  ·Support  UAT (User Acceptance Testing) by preparing test cases, coordinating with stakeholders, and ensuring requirements are met.  ·Assist in  data migration, integration requirements, and system documentation  .  ·Provide  production support and troubleshooting  for Salesforce issues.  ·Maintain clear documentation including  BRDs, FRDs, user stories, and process diagrams  .  ·Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive  continuous improvement and system optimization  .  Required Qualifications:   ·3–6 years of experience  as a Business Analyst with  Salesforce platform exposure  .  ·Strong understanding of  Salesforce Sales Cloud and/or Service Cloud  .  ·Experience with  requirements gathering, documentation, and stakeholder management  .  ·Knowledge of  Agile/Scrum methodologies  .  ·Ability to create  user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional specifications  .  ·Experience with  Salesforce reporting, dashboards, and basic configuration  .  ·Strong  analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em nova odessa. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Confira a vaga para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em gaspar. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

Are you a Portuguese speaker who graduated as an English Teacher? We are looking for you!Teach fun English classes online via Zoom from the comfort of your own home! You can set your own hours and teach on the go as long as you have a solid color backdrop, a laptop, good Wi Fi, a webcam, and a microphone.  If you love teaching, but dread prepping for lessons and grading, this is the perfect job for you. We provide our teachers with all the lesson materials so all you have to do is show up for class and do what you do best, which is teach! Whether you’re looking for a second stream of income or a full-time job, we’ve got you covered. You can work as little as 16 hours a month up to as much as 30 hours a week. You will be scheduled shifts two weeks in advance according to the availability you provide us and we also offer the flexibility of dropping shifts and picking up extra shifts.  If you are busier one week, you can drop some of your shifts and have other teachers help you out or if you want to earn more $$ another week, you can pick up extra shifts and help other teachers out.  When you are on shift, you log on to our platform and teach the lessons provided as well as write short feedback for the students after class. Simple as that! In short, here are some reasons why you will love working as an Online English Teacher with Latin Hire:   Up to 30 hours of shifts available per week! You be your own boss and set your own schedule  Work from anywhere (as long as you have good Wi Fi, workspace, computer, webcam, and microphone). Access to a computer with a reliable, high-speed (at least 2 MB) internet connection.  Must pass a criminal background check.  Teachers must provide at least ten (10) hours of weekly availability.    Who we are:   Established in 2003, Latin Hire recruits and manages teams of subject matter experts (SMEs) for online education companies. title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em piracicaba. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position. If you love teaching, but dread prepping for lessons and grading, this is the perfect job for you. We provide our teachers with all the lesson materials so all you have to do is show up for class and do what you do best, which is teach! Whether you’re looking for a second stream of income or a full-time job, we’ve got you covered. You can work as little as 16 hours a month up to as much as 30 hours a week.  What is a typical day for an Online English Teacher at Latin Hire?  You will be scheduled shifts two weeks in advance according to the availability you provide us and we also offer the flexibility of dropping shifts and picking up extra shifts.  If you are busier one week, you can drop some of your shifts and have other teachers help you out or if you want to earn more $$ another week, you can pick up extra shifts and help other teachers out.  When you are on shift, you log on to our platform and teach the lessons provided as well as write short feedback for the students after class. Simple as that! In short, here are some reasons why you will love working as an Online English Teacher with Latin Hire:   Up to 30 hours of shifts available per week! You be your own boss and set your own schedule  Work from anywhere (as long as you have good Wi Fi, workspace, computer, webcam, and microphone).  Depending on the number of hours you decide to teach and on your schedule, you can earn up to USD 900+ per month.    Minimum Requirements:   Portuguese as a first language.  C1 or C2 Level English Speaker  University degree in English Teaching or related area.  One year of experience in teaching English as a foreign language.  Access to a computer with a reliable, high-speed (at least 2 MB) internet connection.  Must pass a criminal background check.  Teachers must provide at least ten (10) hours of weekly availability.    Who we are:   Established in 2003, Latin Hire recruits and manages teams of subject matter experts (SMEs) for online education companies. For over 20 years, our teams have played key roles in the backend of very successful educational startups.
